messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: oncall (alice) — High latency detected on model-serving-prod pool. p99 > 5s, alert threshold breached. Investigate.

Alice Nguyen: Ack'd. I'm on it. Pulling up dashboards + logs.

Alice Nguyen: Quick summary — p95 jumped from ~200ms to 1.2s and p99 spiked to ~8s around 16:12 UTC. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers (stream chunk gaps ~3–6s). Tagging infra.

Ben Ortiz: Looking at node metrics now. I'm seeing one host (gpunode-12) with GPU memory pinned ~98% and very high write bandwidth on NVMe (~700 MB/s). IO wait on that host elevated.

Carlos Mendez: Also seeing increased grpc tail latency on runtime-worker pods on that node. KV cache lookups timeouts rising. Could be multi-tenant noisy neighbor hitting shared NVMe or bus.

Alice Nguyen: Any deployments/rollouts around that time? deploy-bot, did something go out?

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: rollout finished for service "batch-encoder" at 16:08 UTC to cluster-east-1. No failures.

Ben Ortiz: batch-encoder had a big shard job scheduled at 16:09 — checking if it landed on gpunode-12.

Ben Ortiz: Yeah — container id 8f1b2c3d on gpunode-12 running a heavy CUDA graph job. It reports repeated cudaMalloc failures but still consuming memory (OOM retries?).

Carlos Mendez: If container isn't releasing pinned buffers, it can push other tenants into swapping or increased NVMe IO (spill to disk). Check cgroup memory.events.

Alice Nguyen: Pulling cgroup stats on gpunode-12:

```
# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/docker/8f1b2c3d/memory.stat
cache 234567890
rss 120345678
swap 0
memory.oom_control 0
memory.events "oom_kill:3 low; memory_pressure:12"
```

Alice Nguyen: swap=0 but memory_pressure ramped. NVMe utilization shows many small writes. Not normal for inference-only workloads.

Dana Lee: Any idea which customer/job that container belongs to? We need to assess customer impact and whether to kill.

Ben Ortiz: Looks like partner-ml's large batch indexing job — started by scheduled workflow. I have the workflow id and owner in the scheduler UI.

Alice Nguyen: Impact: routing to model-serving-prod on that node has increased latency and streaming stalls. Risk of request timeouts. Affected customers: 3 active customers in that AZ (IDs redacted). CS has been notified.

Carlos Mendez: Mitigations we can try in order:
1) Remove noisy container from shared pool (stop container or set cpuset/cgroup limits).
2) Drain gpunode-12 and migrate runtime pods off it.
3) Route traffic away from cluster-east-1 to fallback pool for critical customers.
4) If needed, scale up dedicated capacity.

Alice Nguyen: I'll attempt a soft mitigation first — throttle the container's IO and CPU using cgroups.

Ben Ortiz: Command to limit IO using iosched (example):

```
# echo "8:0 rbps=100mb wbps=100mb" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/8f1b2c3d/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```

Ben Ortiz: And set CPU shares lower:

```
# echo 256 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/docker/8f1b2c3d/cpu.shares
```

Alice Nguyen: Applied IO throttle and reduced cpu.shares. Monitoring metrics.

Carlos Mendez: I'm seeing p95 drop back toward 400ms within 30s. p99 coming down too (now ~2.1s). NVMe write bw for that container dropped to ~120 MB/s.

Dana Lee: Good. Any streaming stalls still? CS reported a couple of 5–10s stalls earlier.

Alice Nguyen: Stalls significantly reduced. Still seeing 1–2 customer streams with brief gaps. Looks like some requests were queued/dropped earlier; retrying should be fine.

Ben Ortiz: We should still evacuate the node to be safe. I'll start cordon + drain of gpunode-12 for runtime pods (not killing the batch job yet) and move critical pods to other nodes.

Ben Ortiz: `kubectl cordon gpunode-12 && kubectl drain gpunode-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

Alice Nguyen: Starting routing adjustments — moving critical customers to model-serving-fallback pool using routing policy override for the next 30m.

Carlos Mendez: Alerting: p99 back under 1.5s for the cluster overall. Streaming lag eliminated for most customers. Marking incident severity de-escalation in notes.

Alice Nguyen: Customer impact: transient increased latency and a few streaming stalls between 16:12–16:20 UTC. No request data loss confirmed. Customers A/B/C affected — CS outreach in progress and they are patching with retries.

Dana Lee: Next steps / follow-up:
- Ben to file infra ticket to limit batch workflows on shared gpu pools and add scheduler affinity rules. (TICKET-INC-4521)
- Carlos to add runtime alert for NVMe write saturation per host.
- Alice to draft post-incident summary and customer communication.

Ben Ortiz: Filed TICKET-INC-4521: "Prevent batch indexing on shared model-serving GPU pools". Added scheduler constraint suggestion: nodeSelector: dedicated=batch-indexers for large batch jobs.

Carlos Mendez: I'll add a Prometheus rule: node_namespace_device:disk_write_bytes > 600MB/s for 2m -> page oncall.

Alice Nguyen: Handing off to @Dana for next shift. Summary attached to the ticket. I'll remain on-call for questions.

Dana Lee: Taking over. Thanks Alice — I'll run through the playbook, verify drains completed, and confirm CS messaging. Quick note: escalate to infra leadership if this recurs within 24h.

Alice Nguyen: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone. Closing active mitigation steps at 16:34 UTC. I'll post a short postmortem draft in #postmortems within the hour.

IncidentBot: Incident notes updated: severity -> mitigated. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TICKET-INC-4521

Dana Lee: Verified drains complete at 16:41 UTC. Node gpunode-12 remains offline for investigation. Leaving follow-ups in the ticket.
